about: Judgements of the claim compiler's reading of each claim in eval/claim-tests-foreign-b.json (set B), scored once with the grammar of 10425c0 (unchanged at 0f8a25c and after): one entry per claim and canonical test printed ('none' when refused). reading: right, wrong (a test that does not mean what the sentence says), or not_compiled; for a claim its author marked numeric, cause says why it did not compile (metric the tool does not have, form it does not have, period it cannot place, phrasing of something it supports). The raw readings were committed first (eval/results/claim-tests-foreign-b-raw.txt) and the grammar was not changed after reading the set. Readings added on 18 November 2026, after the measure catalogue (app.core.measures) widened the grammar, are judged by the same session that wrote the catalogue and say so ('catalogue, 18 November 2026'); no earlier judgement was changed.
judge: the grammar's author (Claude Opus 5.5 session), 18 November 2026; an independent judge's file is eval/results/claim-foreign-b-for-judge.md

judgements.why: yoy(revenue)[FY2026] > 50% is a supported test; 'well over' and the trailing comment 'extending a run of exceptional growth' are not explained
sequential revenue growth is supported, but 'again' says it also rose the quarter before (a streak of two), which the grammar does not read
a sub-segment's revenue (Data Center compute against networking) in every quarter: no such measure, and the each-period form is not supported either
gross profit above $100 billion in fiscal 2026: exactly the sentence
net_margin > 50% is supported; the opening comment 'the margins are absurd' made the compiler stop at an unnamed margin (its stated reason misleads)
'net cash provided by operating activities' is operating cash flow under its statement name, which the grammar does not know
two statements; the second needs SG&A, which is not in the metric set
purchases of property and equipment AND intangible assets is broader than capex; no such measure
shareholders' equity is not in the metric set
inventory more than doubling over the year is a supported growth threshold on inventory; 'ended the year at over twice the prior-year balance' is not read
how many customers exceed 10% is a count of tagged customers, not a form; only the largest customer's share is read
a segment's share under 3% is the supported share form; the opening comment 'is a rounding error,' breaks the anchored share sentence
diluted EPS above $2.50 is supported; the two-digit period 'FY25' is not placed
operating expenses as a share of revenue is not in the metric set (only R&D's share is)
faster growth in each of the last two fiscal years: the each-period form is not supported
buybacks and dividends are not in the metric set
cash plus marketable securities, and debt, are not in the metric set
the tax provision and pre-tax income are not in the metric set
a half year (first half of fiscal 2026) is not a period this version places
cost of revenue is not in the metric set; a causal comment follows
says growth slowed without saying growth of what; the refusal is right, the claim is underspecified
accounts payable is not in the metric set
interest income and interest expense are not in the metric set
goodwill is not in the metric set
free cash flow margin above 40% over the trailing twelve months
a segment's revenue growth: breakdowns have no history in the facts
